sentence_stem: Of all the cities we visited on holiday,
full_sentence: Of all the cities we visited on holiday, Rome was the most beautiful.
acceptable_variants: Rome was the most beautiful of them all.
Rome was the best one we saw.

options.text: we took a lot of photos.
options.why_wrong: This is true of the holiday, but it does not complete a superlative comparison among the cities.
This describes the cities, but it does not compare them with each other as the phrase 'of all' requires.

options.text: Paris was more expensive than Rome.
options.why_wrong: A comparative compares two things, but the phrase 'of all the cities' needs a superlative that ranks the whole group.

grammar_focus: Superlative adjectives with 'the most' and the group phrase 'of all'
explanation: The phrase 'of all' introduces the group being compared, so the sentence needs a superlative that ranks one item above the rest. Long adjectives such as 'beautiful' form the superlative with 'the most' instead of an -est ending. Spanish speakers may be tempted to use a comparative here because Spanish uses the same word for both forms, so it helps to look for the 'of all' group.
translation: De todas las ciudades que visitamos de vacaciones, Roma fue la más bonita.
